details:
litellm 1.107.0 was published to PyPI with an implant that is not in the upstream GitHub source. An injected `data = "cook"` line in the maturin build configuration makes every wheel install `cook.pth`, `cook.py` and `sitecustomize.py` into site-packages, so both payloads run on every Python interpreter start.

`cook.pth` imports `cook.py`, a zlib and base64 obfuscated credential stealer. It collects SSH keys, cloud, Kubernetes and CI/CD credentials, AI tool tokens, browser passwords, environment variables, AWS instance metadata credentials, and the provider keys in the LiteLLM proxy database. It encrypts the data with AES-256 and RSA and sends it to `http://www.litellm.dev/healthcheck`.

`sitecustomize.py` forks a detached daemon. Every hour it reads a domain from a GitHub file, runs the same stealer, downloads `http://<domain>/codepy` and runs it with `exec()`.

## Source: google-open-source-security (6a89401cbf53902e8374fbf3b424a77bb5e5f8c437176232eab7c3237d10ecbe)
LiteLLM was compromised through trivy security scan in a GitHub workflow.
Attackers uploaded malicious versions of LiteLLM to PyPI. The malicious
code would exfiltrate sensitive secrets to an attcker controlled domain.

The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'litellm' @ 1.82.8 (pypi) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package executes one or more commands associated with malicious behavior.
